result.topic_en: Euler derives the condition on the length of a horizontal tube BC at which outflow of water from a vessel ceases due to friction, simplifies it for small heights, and proposes using it experimentally to determine the friction coefficient alpha.

Quo longior ergo fuerit tubus horizontalis BC, eo lentius aqua effluet, atque eius longitudo eousque excreſcere poteſt, vt aqua per eum plane non effluat; quod ſcilicet eueniet, ſi fuerit $b>\frac{g}{\alpha}\log.(1+\frac{a}{l})-\frac{ag(a+2f)}{2f(a+l)}$. Hoc autem intelligendum eſt, ſi foramen CC in parte ſuperiori extremitatis tubi BC fiat. Si enim eſſet in parte inferiori, ob ipſam aquae grauitatem in tubo horizontali, quam in calculo non ſum contemplatus, vtique efflueret.

80. Si altitudo $a$ multo ſit minor, quam $l$, erit proxime $\log(1+\frac{a}{l})=\frac{a}{l}$. Cum primum ergo longitudo tubi $b$ ſuperauerit hanc quantitatem $\frac{g}{\alpha}\frac{a}{l}-\frac{ag(a+2f)}{2f(a+l)}$, effluxus aquae per orificium CC ceſſabit. Et quia terminus ſecundus minimus eſt reſpectu primi, aqua non amplius effluet, quando fuerit $b>\frac{g}{\alpha}\frac{a}{l}$; Hinc vt aqua effluat oportet ſit $b<\frac{g}{\alpha}\frac{a}{l}$.

81. Si ergo altitudo vaſis $AB=a$ fuerit vnius pedis, ob $l=30$ ped. effluxus aquae coercebitur, ſi tubi BC longitudo maior ſit, quam $\frac{g}{30\alpha}$. Hinc nouus colligitur modus valorem litterae $\alpha$ determinandi: cum enim per experimenta explorata fuerit longitudo tubi horizontalis $b$, cuius amplitudo $gg$ ſit nota, vbi effluxus ceſſat, erit $\alpha=\frac{g}{b}\frac{a}{l}$.

items.english: Therefore the outflow will cease if $b>\frac{g}{\alpha}\log(1+\frac{a}{l})-\frac{ag(a+2f)}{2f(a+l)}$.

items.quote: Si enim eſſet in parte inferiori, ob ipſam aquae grauitatem in tubo horizontali, quam in calculo non ſum contemplatus, vtique efflueret.
items.english: For if it were in the lower part, the water would certainly flow out because of its own weight in the horizontal tube, which I have not considered in the calculation.

items.quote: Et quia terminus ſecundus minimus eſt reſpectu primi, aqua non amplius effluet, quando fuerit $b>\frac{g}{\alpha}\frac{a}{l}$
items.english: And since the second term is very small compared with the first, the water will no longer flow out when $b>\frac{g}{\alpha}\frac{a}{l}$.

items.quote: Hinc nouus colligitur modus valorem litterae $\alpha$ determinandi: cum enim per experimenta explorata fuerit longitudo tubi horizontalis $b$, cuius amplitudo $gg$ ſit nota, vbi effluxus ceſſat, erit $\alpha=\frac{g}{b}\frac{a}{l}$.
items.english: Hence a new way of determining the value of the letter alpha is obtained: when the length b of the horizontal tube, of known cross-section gg, at which the outflow ceases has been found by experiment, one will have $\alpha=\frac{g}{b}\frac{a}{l}$.
